final_answer:
Two high-risk user requirements are not currently verified: **URS-EBR-009** and **URS-INC-004**.

**URS-EBR-009** (Target MOI outside 4.0–6.0 TU/cell shall be rejected for GMP runs) has no executed verification. It is linked to high-risk assessment FRA-042 (RPN 108 via FM-05) and is traced down to CS-EBR-03 (the MOI range-check configuration). No test case in the database verifies CS-EBR-03 or URS-EBR-009. The only related test, TC-OQ-EBR-04, verifies the vector-volume calculation (URS-EBR-007), not the range rejection. The requirement therefore has no test evidence.

**URS-INC-004** (door-open alarm within 60 s) has a failed verification that was never closed by a passing retest. TC-OQ-INC-04 passed on INC-01, INC-02 and INC-04. On INC-03 it failed (alarm at 142 s against a limit of 60 s, execution TX-0023). Deviation DEV-26-011 records this as "INC-03 door alarm function not verified" (root cause: door switch misaligned). The deviation is marked closed, but no passing re-execution exists for INC-03. The same INC-03 door problem recurred in PPQ26-02 (DEV-26-033, door found not fully latched), which reinforces that the requirement is not verified for that unit.

The other 24 high-risk requirements (those linked to HIGH-class risks via FRA assessments or PFMEA mitigations) all have passing executions. Several of them, including URS-EBR-001, URS-EMS-011, URS-EMS-012, URS-EMS-014, URS-LIMS-002, URS-LIMS-003 and URS-LIMS-004, are verified only through a child specification (TRACE link) rather than a direct VERIFIES link. I treated those as verified because the test cases pass and their acceptance criteria match the requirement. If your procedure requires direct VERIFIES links to the URS, those would need to be added, but they are not missing evidence.
